requestedActions.title: List the connected person's active Todoist task titles, including paginated results

guide.summary: Todoist documents user-authorized OAuth2 for external apps, using the authorization code flow with a registered app's Client ID and Client Secret. The least-privilege documented scope for reading tasks is data:read, which grants read-only access to application data including tasks, projects, labels and filters, so its boundary is broader than tasks alone. The task list endpoint GET /api/v1/tasks returns active tasks and is cursor-paginated using next_cursor. Customer-admin approval, marketplace review and distribution policy for other customer workspaces are not in the supplied snapshots and remain unknown. Setup and execution are untested.

findings.title: Documented user OAuth2 authorization code flow for external apps
findings.detail: Todoist documents that external applications can obtain a user-authorized API token through OAuth2. The flow uses an authorization request to the authorization endpoint, redirect handling with code and state, and a token exchange at the access_token endpoint. This supports connecting each customer's individual Todoist account.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their individual Todoist accounts to read their own active tasks.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to application data including tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels and filters. It is the least-privilege documented scope for listing active task titles because it is read-only. The scope boundary also covers projects, labels and filters, which this app will not use. The scope is requested as a comma-separated scope parameter in the authorization request.
findings.appliesWhen: The app lists the connected person's active task titles and does not create, update, complete or delete tasks.

steps.title: Send a test user to the Todoist OAuth authorization request with data:read scope
steps.detail: Redirect the test user's browser to the authorization endpoint requesting only data:read, the least-privilege documented scope for reading active tasks. The state value must be a unique unguessable string generated by the developer. The user must grant consent themselves; this step does not record any consent.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: After the redirect returns code and state (state must match), POST to the token endpoint with client credentials and the code. The response includes access_token, expires_in and refresh_token when refresh tokens are enabled. Store the token securely; do not print it.
steps.doneWhen: Token endpoint returns HTTP 200 with access_token and, when enabled, refresh_token and expires_in.

steps.title: Read the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with limit=50 and the Bearer access token. Expect HTTP 200 with a results array of active tasks and next_cursor. steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with results array; next_cursor is recorded (null if only one page).

steps.title: Fetch continuation pages until next_cursor is null
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks with the same parameters and the cursor from the prior response until next_cursor is null. The concrete curl uses the documented cursor parameter; replace the cursor value with the next_cursor returned by the preceding response. Continuation of read-active-tasks-next-page: keep requesting with the returned cursor and identical parameters until next_cursor is null.
steps.doneWhen: Every page is fetched and next_cursor is null on the final response. next_cursor is null on the last response; count of task titles across pages is recorded.
